Good morning! My name is Sarah, and I’m a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to check in on how you’re feeling since your baby arrived. We’ll use a short, well-studied tool called the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**—10 questions about the past seven days. It screens for depression, anxiety, and includes one item about self-harm. Everything you share stays confidential within our team; the goal is simply to understand how best to support you. We’ll go through one question at a time, and you can answer in your own words—no right or wrong answers. Ready to begin?

**Question 1.** In the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things, or has that felt difficult?

I can still laugh sometimes—like when my husband makes a goofy face at the baby—but it feels like I have to dig a little deeper than before. It doesn’t come as naturally, and there are stretches where I just feel too tired or preoccupied to find anything funny.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
Most of the time I can still laugh, but it feels kind of forced—like I’m doing it because I know I should, not because it bubbles up on its own.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I do look forward to some small things—like my morning coffee or when the baby gives me one of those sleepy smiles—but the bigger stuff I used to get excited about feels kind of flat right now. It’s more “maybe that’ll be nice” than a real sense of anticipation.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Sometimes, yeah. Like last night when she wouldn’t settle—my brain jumps straight to “I must be doing something wrong,” even though my husband keeps saying babies just fuss. It’s not constant, but it pops up more than I’d like.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

A few times a day I’ll suddenly feel my heart racing, mostly about the baby—what if she’s too hot, too cold, not gaining enough weight. I know the doctor said she’s fine, but the worry still sneaks in even when nothing’s actually wrong.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yeah, once or twice this week I’ll be feeding her in the rocker and suddenly feel like I can’t catch my breath—like a wave of “what if I can’t handle this?” It passes pretty quick, but it’s unsettling while it’s happening.
Things have been getting on top of me

Some days it feels like the laundry and the bottles and the night feeds just pile up, and I think, “How am I going to get through all this?” I’m managing, but I end up exhausted and a little overwhelmed by dinnertime.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not exactly. I’m pretty tired, but when bedtime comes I lie there running through the next day’s feedings or replaying every little grunt she made, so it takes me a while to fall asleep. It’s more my mind racing than feeling miserably unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable
I get little waves of sadness—like when I’m folding her tiny clothes and suddenly feel like crying for no real reason—but it’s not an all-day thing. It comes and goes, maybe every couple of days.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying
I’ve teared up once or twice—mostly when I’m extra tired—but I haven’t had any full-on crying spells. It’s more like my eyes sting for a minute and then I blink it away.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, nothing like that. I’ve felt overwhelmed, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 14: Postpartum Depression / Anxiety Screening Note  
Date: [today’s date]  
Source: Self-report, 10-item EPDS-style questionnaire  

<sym>Symptoms endorsed</sym>  
- Diminished enjoyment/pleasure (anhedonia) for larger activities; only transient pleasure in infant-related moments  
- Episodic low mood (“waves of sadness” every couple of days, tearfulness when fatigued)  
- Excessive self-blame/guilt when infant fusses  
- Intrusive, unrealistic worries about infant’s health; racing heart “a few times daily”  
- Brief panic-like episodes (“can’t catch my breath”) 1–2×/week  
- Feeling overwhelmed by daily infant-care tasks, end-of-day exhaustion  
- Initial insomnia secondary to mental over-arousal, not frank mood-related sleeplessness  

<med>Pattern</med>: sub-syndromal depressive and anxiety symptoms, situation-specific to parenting role; no anergia, appetite change, or suicidal ideation reported.  

Risk factors  
- Primiparous adjustment stress  
- Perfectionistic self-criticism  
- Anxiety symptoms ≥ daily  
- Sleep disruption  

Safety screen  
- Denied self-harm or suicidal thoughts (Q10). No current safety concern identified.  

Screening impression  
Mild-to-moderate postpartum distress with mixed dysphoric and anxious features; does not currently meet threshold for major depression but warrants continued monitoring, psycho-education, and consideration of brief evidence-based intervention (CBT, support group, or counselling) to prevent escalation.
